snacs-adaptation-notes.txt:
SNACS v2.6: label each target [scene role, lexical function], both p.-prefixed. Scene role is the contextual relation; function is the marker's conventional meaning. Use the same label when no construal is needed.

Temporal and spatial: 'a few years since I have been' = p.Time/p.Time; 'after relocating' and 'after our meal' = p.Time/p.Time; 'in the morning' = p.Time/p.Time; 'throughout the year' = p.Duration/p.Duration. Ordinary temporal adpositions do not get spatial construals just because a metaphor is imaginable. 'Relocating to South Bend' = p.Goal/p.Goal; 'get it back' = p.Direction/p.Direction; 'at the bottom' = p.Locus/p.Locus; 'slapped pieces of wood over' = p.Goal/p.Locus.

Possessives: determine the noun's relation, never default all possessives to Possessor. 'Stuart's strategies' = p.Gestalt/p.Gestalt; 'our business' and 'my gym' where the person belongs to the organization = p.OrgMember/p.Possessor and p.OrgMember/p.Gestalt respectively, following each attested case; 'your contributions,' 'their service,' and 'our meal' where the possessor performs or provides the event = p.Agent/p.Gestalt; 'my waitress' and 'my friend' = p.SocialRel/p.Gestalt; 'your money' and 'your time' = p.Possessor/p.Possessor.

Argument and participant uses: 'rewards of this program' = p.Force/p.Force (program as causal source); 'each of you' = p.QuantityItem/p.Whole; 'proud of your contributions' = p.Stimulus/p.Topic; 'recommend this place to anyone' = p.Recipient/p.Goal. 'Wait for my waitress,' 'bother with this,' 'ask for the dinner combo,' and 'look for an establishment' = p.Theme/p.Theme.

Other attested distinctions: 'for New Year's Eve dinner' modifies an establishment's intended use = p.Purpose/p.Purpose; infinitival 'to try' in 'slapped pieces of wood over to try to cover it up' = p.Purpose/p.Purpose. 'Something like smorgasbord' and 'huge experience for such a small salon' = p.ComparisonRef/p.ComparisonRef; 'look like they were flooded' = p.Theme/p.ComparisonRef. 'A variety of many kinds of things' uses both of markers as p.Species/p.Species. 'Pieces of wood' = p.Stuff/p.Stuff. Keep contextual comparison, kind/category, and material relations distinct.

Guideline exceptions retained: 'sleeping through the night' = p.Duration/p.Duration. Directional temporal use can be p.Time/p.Direction, e.g. 'schedule the appointment for Monday.' Genitives have broad Gestalt or Possessor functions while their contextual scene roles can be Agent, OrgMember, Whole, and others. Decide by semantic relation, not surface form alone.
